text: APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software programs to communicate with each other. When you work with an API, you typically send an HTTP request to a server, asking for data or an action. The server then responds, often in a format called JSON, which is easy for computers to read and organize. Most APIs require authentication, usually through a special key, to ensure only authorized users access their data. It's also important to respect rate limits, which are rules about how many requests you can make in a certain time period—sending too many can block your access. Finally, always plan for error handling. Network issues or server problems can occur, so your code should catch errors and respond gracefully, rather than crashing.
